Method of Attack: Process hollowing: malware starts a legitimate process, suspends it, empties its memory space, copies malicious code inside, then resumes the process to execute malicious code

Atom bombing: malware stores malicious code inside atom tables (shared memory tables) and uses lesser known Windows APIs to execute it, tricking AV or OS-whitelisted apps into executing malicious operations
Indicators of Compromise: Use of process hollowing and atom bombing code injection techniques
Attack Vector: Code injection via process hollowing and atom bombing techniques
